Main charitable entity types: Associations / third-sector organisations (Act 110/2021); non-business foundations (sjálfseignarstofnanir, Act 19/1988 as am. by Act 112/2024; charter approved by the District Commissioner) or business foundations (Act 33/1999); tax-deductible status via Skatturinn's public-benefit register (almannaheillaskrá).
Est. cost & time: Association registration about ISK 5,000-10,000; 2-4 weeks. Foundations require a minimum endowment of about ISK 1,000,000; foreigners may found.
Key local requirements: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation requires ~ISK 3m endowment and Icelandic management
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Icelandic registered address, Icelandic-language documents, ~5 members; tax exemption is a separate application.
Notes: Documents in Icelandic; tax-deductible status requires registration on Skatturinn's public-benefit register; small bureaucracy but limited English support | verify-rest 2026-10: charitable foundations fall under Act 19/1988 (Act 33/1999 is for business foundations); third-sector Act 110/2021; RSK is now Skatturinn

Main charitable entity types: Associations (yhdistys, 3+ founders, Associations Act 503/1989); foundations (säätiö, Foundations Act 487/2015, EUR 50,000 minimum capital); registered with PRH. Charitable status via the Tax Administration.
Est. cost & time: PRH registration fee about EUR 100; 1-3 months. Foreigners may be members; no residency requirement to found an association.
Key local requirements: Finnish address; association needs 3+ founding members; foundation needs EUR 50,000 minimum basic capital (PRH fee ~EUR 920) and an EEA-resident board
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Finnish registered address + local service recipient; Finnish/Swedish-language statutes; PRH processing slow.
Notes: Finnish-language requirement for documents and minutes; PRH bureaucracy is the main burden; foundations are hard for a foreign founder | confirm prior; PRH registration fee is about EUR 100. | verify-rest 2026-10: association needs 3 founders; foundation minimum capital EUR 50,000

Main charitable entity types: Ideell förening (non-profit association; organisation number from Skatteverket, form SKV 8400, free); ekonomisk förening (registered at Bolagsverket); stiftelse (foundation, county administrative board).
Est. cost & time: About SEK 1,000-2,500; 4-8 weeks. A bank account needs a D-number. Foreigners may be members; no residency rule for founding.
Registration fee (USD): $0 for an ideell förening (Skatteverket); ~$180-210 for an ekonomisk förening (SEK 1,900 online)
Key local requirements: Swedish registered seat (säte) and min. 3 members for the association, no residency requirement; foundation needs ~SEK 250k+ and a Swedish-resident board
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Swedish registered seat (säte) required; board residency not required; Bolagsverket online registration.
Notes: Straightforward online registration with Bolagsverket, English widely understood; a Swedish bank account for the entity typically requires a personal/D-number for the signatory | verify-rest 2026-10: ideell förening gets its org. number from Skatteverket free; Bolagsverket fee applies only to economic associations

Main charitable entity types: Voluntary associations (frivillige foreninger); foundations; associations registered with the CVR register. The Act on Foundations and Certain Associations (LBK nr. 2020 of 11/12/2020, as amended) applies to foundations.
Est. cost & time: Association registration at CVR is free; DKK 0-2,000 total with legal support; 2-6 weeks. Foundations Act (LBK 2020/2020) requires a Danish-resident board majority.
Key local requirements: Danish address, min. 2 members, registered in the CVR register; Foundations Act (LBK 2020/2020) requires a Danish-resident board majority for foundations
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Danish registered address required; CVR registration is needed to receive 30A deductible donations.
Notes: Association name and documents must be in Danish; CVR registration itself is easy; Danish-controlled foundation rules make the foundation route hard for a foreigner | verify-rest 2026-10: LB 938/2012 superseded by consolidated LBK nr. 2020 of 11/12/2020

Main charitable entity types: Associations (biedrības) and foundations (nodibinājumi) under the Associations and Foundations Law (adopted 30 Oct 2003, in force 1 Apr 2004), registered in the Enterprise Register via the e-portal.
Est. cost & time: State fee EUR 11.38 (10% less online); total EUR 30-100; 1-4 weeks. E-filing with an e-signature avoids the notary step. A Latvian address is required.
Key local requirements: Latvian address and Latvian-language name/documents; e-filing via registrs.ur.gov.lv with a Latvian/EU e-signature needs no notary (paper filings need notarised signatures)
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Latvian address, Latvian-resident board, and Latvian e-ID for filing — a local representative is mandatory
Notes: Associations and foundations share one law (2003); e-filing with an EU e-signature avoids the notary, otherwise notarised signatures force an in-person visit or a local representative | NVO registers electronically via e-portals; no notary step needed. Real barriers: Latvian-resident board requirement plus local address and e-ID | verify-rest 2026-10: law date corrected to 2003/2004; no '2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law' exists; state fee EUR 11.38 (Cabinet Reg. 308)

Main charitable entity types: Fundação (private foundation recognised by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers under the Lei-Quadro das Fundações, Lei 24/2012) and Associação (association)
Est. cost & time: €1,000–€2,500 (notary, legal, fees); ~1–2 months for notarisation and public-interest status
Registration fee (USD): none (nominal registration; ~$1,100-2,800 total incl. notary and legal)
Key local requirements: Portuguese registered office and a locally-based responsible party/director; notarised foundation deed; patrimonial sufficiency presumed only above the Portaria 75/2013 threshold (reported as EUR 250,000 for national-scope foundations)
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Needs Portuguese registered office and locally-based responsible officer; public-interest status approval is discretionary.
Notes: The most straightforward of the four for a foreign founder: no citizenship/residency requirement for the founder, and no fixed minimum capital. However, to be treated as an entity of public interest (required for tax-exempt status and grants) it needs an endowment and approval by the relevant authority. English filings are not routine; use a Portuguese lawyer. A local office can be provided by a law firm or registered agent, which is what keeps this at medium rather than easy. | verify-rest 2026-10: 'no statutory minimum endowment' corrected — Portaria 75/2013 sufficiency threshold applies; 'Instituto' is not a separate private form

Main charitable entity types: No ordinary commercial/charitable registry; charitable activity is conducted through pontifical institutions, canonically erected entities, or bodies recognised by the Holy See (e.g., pontifical foundations/works) rather than a self-service registration
Est. cost & time: No fixed fee or standard timeline; entirely case-by-case at the discretion of the Holy See
Key local requirements: No independent self-registration pathway; any entity operating on Vatican territory must be recognised/erected by the Holy See (competent dicastery/pontifical authority) and be compliant with the Fundamental Law of the Vatican City State
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): No self-service registry exists; any entity must be erected/recognised by the Holy See at its sole discretion.
Notes: The Vatican does not operate a conventional commercial-law or charity-registration framework open to foreign founders. There is no public registry an Australian-resident can simply file into. Charitable or philanthropic activity on Vatican territory is established by canonical/pontifical act (e.g., erection or recognition of a pontifical work), which requires a direct relationship with the appropriate Holy See authority and is typically reserved for Church-linked bodies. For a private foreign founder there is effectively no independent, self-service charitable-entity route; the realistic option is to establish the charity in Italy (or elsewhere) and, if relevant, seek a canonical relationship with the Holy See. | confirm prior: no ordinary charity registry, no fixed fee or timeline, very hard difficulty all accurate.

Main charitable entity types: Associations under the Ottoman Law of Associations of 3 Aug 1909 (notification 'ilm wa khabar' to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Circular 10/AM/2006); foundations.
Est. cost & time: About USD 100-500; 2-6 weeks. Foreigners may found and direct associations; the notification regime is less formal than a full registration system.
Key local requirements: Foreigners may participate, but foreign-controlled associations may be treated as foreign associations needing separate authorization; local registered office, Arabic founding documents and a local signatory; notification regime, not pre-approval
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local registered office, local signatory, Arabic documents; bank-account opening friction
Notes: Legally one of the easiest for foreigners in the region, but heavy Arabic-only bureaucracy, bank-account opening friction, and macro instability (currency, banking) make practical setup harder; most internationals use a local registered partner or a foundation | Confirm prior: foreigners may found/direct, notification regime, 2-6 weeks; banking is the practical friction | verify-rest 2026-10: 'no nationality rule' softened — foreign-controlled associations may require authorization

Main charitable entity types: Association or private institution under Law No. 93 of 1958 (am. Legislative Decree 224/1969), registered with the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor
Est. cost & time: Nominally low fees, 1-4 months in a stable environment; currently not practically achievable remotely
Key local requirements: Local registration, local address and signatories; MoSAL directive of 1 Oct 2025 requires prior approval for foreign affiliations/funding; replacement associations law still only a draft; in-person steps in Syria; sanctions complicate cross-border funding
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): In-person steps, local signatory/office; OFAC sanctions block USD funding and banking channels
Notes: Civil-society registration resumed after 2025 transition (586 NGOs registered by Feb 2025) but framework unstable; sanctions exposure for foreign founders and their banks; English support effectively unavailable; advise against direct formation | verify-rest 2026-10: no new associations law enacted — Law 93/1958 still governs

Main charitable entity types: Non-governmental organisations under Law 12 of 2010, registered with the NGOs Department of the Secretariat General of the Council of Ministers (Kurdistan Region: KRG Law 1/2011).
Est. cost & time: Fees low, but registration requires Iraqi-national or Iraq-resident founders, so non-resident foreigners cannot found directly. Official processing times unpublished.
Key local requirements: Application signed by at least 3 founders who are Iraqi nationals or Iraq residents (foreigners need a valid residence card); local address; Arabic filings
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Founders must be Iraqi nationals (min 10), local board/address, Arabic filings, MoSAL activity approvals
Notes: Resident-expat route is the standard workaround (Iraqi-resident staff as founders); foreign funding rules restrict donor channels; English commonly understood in NGO sector but filings in Arabic; security considerations for in-person steps | Confirm prior: Law 12/2010 governs (new draft NGO law with 5 founders approved but 12/2010 still applied) | verify-rest 2026-10: registering body is the Council of Ministers Secretariat NGO Department; no 10-founder minimum (3 resident/national founders)

Main charitable entity types: Association (Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958, am. Law 75-00 of 2002; declaration at prefecture); Cooperatives (Law 112-12, am. Law 74-16); foreign associations need Interior Ministry permit
Est. cost & time: Registration free (fees unpublished); notary/deed ~US$100-300; 1-3 months; foreign associations face extra Interior Ministry authorization
Key local requirements: Moroccan registered office, Arabic statutes, wilaya/provincial governor approval; foreign founders permitted.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Registered office + Arabic statutes; governor discretion can delay; local address agent usually needed
Notes: Governor discretion can delay approvals; most expats register via a local address agent; Arabic mandatory. | Confirm prior with correction: governing text is Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958 (not 'Law 1956'); foreign founders permitted; 1-3 months realistic | verify-rest 2026-10: cooperatives governed by Law 112-12 (not 19-00)

Main charitable entity types: Local CSO and foreign CSO/NGO (CSO Proclamation No. 1113/2019; registration with the Authority for Civil Society Organizations (ACSO); a restrictive 2025 amendment bill not known to be enacted)
Est. cost & time: Registration ~US$200-500 via local partner/agent; 3-6 months; foreign CSOs register via country office and local representation
Key local requirements: A local organization may be formed by Ethiopians and/or foreigners resident in Ethiopia; non-resident foreigners must work through a partner organization or a registered foreign CSO.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Domestic CSOs require Ethiopian-national founders/members; a foreign founder can only register a foreign NGO office, which needs a local entity and CSO Agency approval.
Notes: 2021 reform liberalised funding and registration, but foreigners cannot directly form a domestic charity; security clearance applies; Amharic/English documents. | verify-rest 2026-10: registrar is ACSO; resident foreigners may co-found local CSOs, non-residents cannot
